Carbon Sequestration and Atmospheric CO2 Analysis

Atmospheric CO2 trends and sequestration method assessment

Generated 2026-10-29T21:22:01.062576+00:00

Executive Summary

This report analyzes 300 monthly NOAA CO2 observations from 2000-01-01 to 2024-12-01.

The estimated compound annual growth rate over the record is 0.57% and the Mann-Kendall test reports a increasing trend (p = 0.0000).

The arima forecast projects 425.04 ppm by the end of the horizon, with a 95% interval of 423.97 to 426.11 ppm.

Leading sequestration options by weighted score: Afforestation and Reforestation (score 0.70), Enhanced Rock Weathering (ERW) (score 0.70), Biochar (score 0.50). Portfolio risk is classified as low.

Introduction and Data Provenance

CO2 concentrations are sourced from the NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory monthly station files. Data are cached with SHA-256 provenance metadata and validated before analysis.

Trend detection combines the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test with OLS and Theil-Sen slope estimates. Forecasts use SARIMA when statsmodels is available and fall back to a seasonal linear model otherwise. Change points are located by binary segmentation using Welch-style mean-shift statistics.

Method comparison normalizes literature-derived cost, permanence, scalability, energy, technology readiness, and risk ranges onto a 0-1 scale, then applies user-configurable weights. These ranges are reference values, not measurements produced by this project.

Method Comparison

Scores are relative to the methods included in this run, so they are not comparable across runs with different method sets.

Pareto analysis identifies methods that are not dominated on both cost and composite benefit. Cost-effectiveness is reported as composite score per USD/tCO2 and should be read alongside permanence and reversal risk.

Limitations and Uncertainties

Correlation between atmospheric CO2 and sequestration deployment does not establish causality. Forecast intervals widen with horizon and assume the estimated model structure remains valid.

Method cost and permanence ranges are drawn from published literature and industry reporting; they vary by location, scale, and accounting boundary. Portfolio simulations are illustrative and do not constitute investment advice.
